checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan: finish in-flight lacon work - align CLI/RLM test expectations with smart shrinking, wire the unused CSV/JSON parsers into Lacon.ask, replace the root-level scratch scripts with real tests, and refresh README test documentation

impact_assessment.why: The working tree fixes two stale assertions but leaves three scratch files at the repository root. unittest discovery imports test_features.py and runs its prints, the CSV/JSON parsers are dead code because ask() still calls sentences(), and JSON parsing drops numeric values. The in-flight work is not honest until the feature is wired and covered.
impact_assessment.benefits: Makes the recently added format parsers reachable through the public API, preserves numeric JSON values, converts manual probes into regression tests, removes root-level test pollution, and keeps README claims accurate.
impact_assessment.risks: Contract: new keyword-only Lacon.ask(context_format=...) defaulting to auto; JSON/CSV contexts now parse structurally instead of as plain sentences. Dependency: stdlib only. Concurrency: none. State: no persisted state changes. A deliberately small context_format value can fall back to text by design.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add tests/test_formats.py for parsers, auto-detection, format answers and the tree-wide budget, plus tests/test_code_understanding.py for AST extraction; run python -m unittest discover and python aikit.py check lacon before committing.

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Milestone 1 completed: wired Lacon.ask to the CSV/JSON/text readers via context_format, kept JSON keys and numeric values, replaced the root scratch scripts with 16 format/code-understanding tests, aligned the shrinking expectations, and refreshed README examples and test coverage notes.

[2/2] Phase 4 verification: python aikit.py check lacon passed 4/4 (test, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); checklists: passed; unittest discovery runs 106 tests green and no longer imports root-level scratch scripts.

[1/3] Plan: add an optional Pebble context format to Lacon. Read .peb source through Pebble's own lexer/parser/AST, turn functions, declarations, loops and comments into evidence sentences, expose context_format=pebble and --context-format, infer it from a .peb file extension, keep the core stdlib-only, add ADR-003, tests and README updates, then run Phase 4 gates.

impact_assessment.why: The two AIKit projects are complementary at the boundary: Pebble has the precise AST and Lacon has budgeted evidence selection. Lacon's current code understanding is Python-only and shallow, while Pebble's parser can supply exact declarations and positions; a narrow adapter adds real structural Q&A without merging the two engines.
impact_assessment.benefits: Lacon gains a second, precise code context; Pebble gains a real consumer; both remain independently testable. Users can ask questions about .peb files offline with an auditable thought script, and Lacon's core stays dependency-free.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a new context_format value, CLI flag, and extension inference change the public surface; dependency: an optional runtime import of the sibling Pebble project, with a clear failure when unavailable; concurrency: none, the adapter is pure and the existing engine is single-threaded; state: no persistence changes, but the module cache and lazy import must not leak a half-initialized package.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Record the contract in ADR-003 before code; make the import lazy and optional; validate formats and surface parse failures as What/Why/Fix with CLI exit 2; add unit tests for conversion, inference, malformed source and the missing-dependency message; run python -m unittest discover and python aikit.py check lacon --no-push.

checkpoints.description: [1/3] complete: added lacon/pebble_context.py with a lazy Pebble import, sibling-checkout discovery, comment/declaration/loop extraction and What/Why/Fix errors; wired context_format=pebble through parse_context and Lacon.ask plus --context-format with .peb inference; expansion now includes the evidence lexicon.

[2/3] complete: 11 adapter tests in tests/test_pebble_context.py cover conversion, parse_context, API answers, CLI inference, forced standard input, malformed source and missing checkout; ADR-003 records the optional boundary; README tree, usage, flags and boundaries updated; codebase map regenerated.

[3/3] complete: Phase 4 gates 4/4 (test 117 passing, hygiene, guidelines/map, secrets); checklists: passed. Uncommitted changes remain: 6 modified and 2 untracked files; delivery is intentionally not pushed.

[review] Second pass fixed the demo flag edge case and added its regression test; 118 tests pass and gates are 4/4. One timing test (tests/test_performance.py::test_lexicon_speed) flaked at 112.9ms when run concurrently with another process, then passed alone; it remains host-sensitive and is out of this task's scope. checklists: passed.

[1/3] Plan: make max_total_chars a hard aggregate cap instead of a pre-node stop; add a regression test that asserts tree_chars <= limit at several ceilings; move host-sensitive wall-clock benchmarks out of the default unittest gate into benchmarks/performance.py; fix the uncollected snake_case test; record ADR-004 (hard cap) and ADR-005 (benchmark placement); refresh README and map; run Phase 4.

impact_assessment.why: Two defects remain from the independent review: a documented tree-wide budget can be exceeded by the root node, and a wall-clock performance test failed the gate once under concurrent load while the suite is supposed to be deterministic. Both undermine the claim that a green gate means a trustworthy result.
impact_assessment.benefits: The budget contract becomes true and testable at the API boundary; the default suite becomes host-independent and faster; the benchmarks remain runnable on demand; the previously uncollected snake_case test becomes part of the regression shield.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: max_total_chars semantics change from best-effort stop to hard cap, and low ceilings may return an empty unknown script; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: benchmark files move and test discovery changes, so README and map must stay synchronized.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Implement a fit-to-remaining helper and reserve one character per ancestor before splitting; test ceilings 0, 1, 8, 50 and a generous limit; keep the benchmarks as an explicit unittest module outside the default test*.py pattern; run the full suite and python aikit.py check lacon --no-push.

checkpoints.description: [1/3] complete: max_total_chars is now a hard aggregate cap. _remaining/_fit fit every node to the remaining tree budget, recursion reserves the node budget and a MIN_CHILD floor for each child, and tests cover ceilings 0,1,8,17,24,50,100,200 plus a generous cap matching the unlimited tree and a negative-cap refusal.

[2/3] complete: moved the seven wall-clock PerformanceTests to benchmarks/performance.py (not collected by unittest discover), left behavior/edge tests in tests/test_performance.py, collected the previously module-level snake_case test, added ADR-004 and ADR-005, and updated README tree/tests/boundaries and the codebase map.

[3/3] complete: Phase 4 gates 4/4 (test 115 passing in 0.3s, hygiene, guidelines/map, secrets); explicit benchmarks 7/7 pass; hard-cap invariants fuzzed across contexts, formats, budgets and caps; checklists: passed. Changes remain uncommitted and unpushed.
